layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In Omnimatte, one aims to decompose a given video into semantically mean-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ingful layers, including the background and individual objects along with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their associated effects, such as shadows and reflections. Existing methods of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ten require extensive training or costly self-supervised optimization. In this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper, we present OmnimatteZero, a training-free approach that leverages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: off-the-shelf pre-trained video diffusion models for omnimatte. It can remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects from videos, extract individual object layers along with their effects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and composite those objects onto new videos. These are accomplished by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapting zero-shot image inpainting techniques for video object removal,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a task they fail to handle effectively out-of-the-box. To overcome this, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduce temporal and spatial attention guidance modules that steer the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion process for accurate object removal and temporally consistent back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground reconstruction. We further show that self-attention maps capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information about the object and its footprints and use them to inpaint the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object's effects, leaving a clean background. Additionally, through simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: latent arithmetic, object layers can be isolated and recombined seamlessly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with new video layers to produce new videos. Evaluations show that Omni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matteZero not only achieves superior performance in terms of background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruction but also sets a new record for the fastest Omnimatte approach,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieving real-time performance with minimal frame runtime. Project Page.

layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extracting or isolating objects in videos is a central problem in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video understanding and editing, with important applications such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as removing, modifying, or enhancing elements within a video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scene. One important flavor of this task is video matting [Chuang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. 2002], which involves decomposing a video into a background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer and one or more foreground layers, each representing an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: individual object. A particularly challenging form of video matting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is Omnimatte [Lu et al. 2021; Wang and Adelson 1994], where each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground object is not only isolated but also includes associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects such as shadows, reflections, and scene perturbations. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers extracted by video matting facilitate various video editing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications, including object removal, background replacement,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retiming [Lu et al. 2020], and object duplication [Lee et al. 2024],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: many of which require estimating occluded background regions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using techniques like video inpainting or omnimatting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, despite their promise, existing methods for video in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: painting and Omnimatte face significant limitations. Recent inpaint-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing approaches [Li et al. 2025; Zhou et al. 2023], while trained on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotated datasets for object removal, fail to account for the nuanced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects that objects impart on the scene. Similarly, current Omni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matte methods demand computationally intensive self-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimization for each video [Lee et al. 2024; Lin et al. 2023; Lu et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2021; Suhail et al. 2023]. Some approaches further rely on large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hand-crafted training datasets [Lee et al. 2024; Winter et al. 2024] or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require 3D scene modeling using meshes or NeRFs [Lin et al. 2023;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Suhail et al. 2023], resulting in hours of training and slow per-frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rendering.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given the success of fast, training-free approaches in image edit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing [Corneanu et al. 2024; Lugmayr et al. 2022], a natural question

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arises: can these methods be effectively adapted to video editing?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we present a new approach called OmnimatteZero,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first training-free generative method to Omnimatte. Omnimat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teZero (named for its zero training and optimization requirements)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leverages off-the-shelf pre-trained video diffusion models to remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all objects from a video, extract individual object layers along with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their associated effects, and finally composite them onto new back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grounds. This entire process is performed efficiently during diffusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference, making it significantly faster than current methods. See

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1 for illustration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We begin by adapting training-free image inpainting methods [Lug

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mayr et al. 2022; Meng et al. 2022] to handle object inpainting in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos using diffusion models. However, we find that simply ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plying these frame-by-frame techniques to videos leads to poor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results: missing regions are not filled convincingly, and temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency breaks down. To address this, we propose two attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guidance modules that can be easily integrated into pre-trained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video diffusion models. These modules guide the diffusion process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to achieve both accurate object removal and consistent background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruction. The first module, Temporal Attention Guidance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (TAG), uses background patches from nearby frames. By modifying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-attention layers, it encourages the model to use these patches to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruct masked regions, improving temporal coherence. The sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ond module, Spatial Attention Guidance (SAG), operates within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each frame to refine local details and enhance visual plausibility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also observe that self-attention maps contain cues not just

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about the object but also its indirect effects, such as shadows and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflections. By leveraging this information, our method can inpaint

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these subtle traces, yielding cleaner backgrounds. For foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer extraction, we find that the object (and its traces) can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isolated by subtracting the latent representation of the clean back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground from the original video latent. This extracted object layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can then be seamlessly inserted into new backgrounds by simply

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adding the latents, enabling fast and flexible video composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To validate our approach, we apply it to two video diffusion mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els, LTXVideo [HaCohen et al. 2024] and Wan2.1 [video 2025], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluate it on standard Omnimatte benchmarks both quantitatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and qualitatively. Our method outperforms all supervised and self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised existing inpainting and Omnimatte techniques across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all benchmarks in terms of background reconstruction and object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer extraction. Notably, OmnimatteZero requires no training or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additional optimization, functioning entirely within the denoising

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process of diffusion models. This positions OmnimatteZero as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fastest Omnimatte technique to date.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 Omnimatte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The first Omnimatte approaches [Kasten et al. 2021; Lu et al. 2021]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use motion cues to decompose a video into RGBA matte layers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assuming a static background with planar homographies. Optimiza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion isolates dynamic foreground layers, taking 3 to 8.5 hours per

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video and ~2.5 seconds per frame to render. Later methods enhanced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Omnimatte with deep image priors [Gu et al. 2023; Lu et al. 2022]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3D representations [Lin et al. 2023; Suhail et al. 2023; Wu et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2024], but still rely on strict motion assumptions and require exten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive training (~6 hours) with rendering times of 2.5-3.5 seconds per

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame. A recent generative approach [Lee et al. 2024] uses video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion priors to remove objects and effects, with test-time op-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timization for frame reconstruction, taking ~9 seconds per frame.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose a novel, training and optimization-free

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method using off-the-shelf video diffusion models, achieving real-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time performance in 0.04 seconds per frame.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2 Video Inpainting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Earlier video inpainting methods [Chang et al. 2019; Hu et al. 2020;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wang et al. 2019] used 3D CNNs for spatiotemporal modeling but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: struggled with long-range propagation due to limited receptive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fields. Pixel-flow approaches [Gao et al. 2020; Zhang et al. 2022a,b]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved texture and detail restoration by utilizing adjacent frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information. Recently, Zhou et al. [2023] introduced ProPainter,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which enhances reconstruction accuracy and efficiency by leverag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing optical flow-based propagation and attention maps. VideoPainter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [Bian et al. 2025] proposed a dual-stream video inpainting method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that injects video context into a pre-trained video diffusion model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using a lightweight encoder. [Li et al. 2025] proposed DiffuEraser,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which combines a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BrushNet, a feature extraction module, to generate temporally con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistent videos. In this paper, we propose a single-step object in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: painting approach, directly applied during video diffusion model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference, implicitly leveraging spatial and temporal information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from adjacent frames for inpainting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3 Diffusion Transformers for Video Generation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent advancements in diffusion models have significantly im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proved text-to-video generation. These models, trained on large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets of video-text pairs, can generate visually compelling videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from text descriptions. Recent work introduced LTX-Video [HaCo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hen et al. 2024], a real-time transformer-based latent diffusion model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capable of generating videos at over 24 frames per second. It builds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on 3D Video-VAE with a spatiotemporal latent space, a concept

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also used in Wan2.1 [video 2025] and the larger HunyuanVideo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [Kong 2024]. Unlike traditional methods that treat the video VAE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and denoising transformer separately, LTX-Video integrates them

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within a highly compressed latent space (1:192 compression ratio),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimizing their interaction. This spatiotemporal downscaling re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sults in 32 × 32 × 8 pixels per token while maintaining high-quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video generation. Similarly, HunyuanVideo employs a large-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Motivation: The failure of image inpainting approaches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We begin by extending training-free image-diffusion inpainting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques to video diffusion models. Our reference point is vanilla

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image inpainting [Lugmayr et al. 2022], a straightforward method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that starts with a random noise at the masked area and, at each dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion step t, injects Gaussian noise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the original background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area so the denoiser can reconstruct the masked region while pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: serving the background during denoising. For video, we apply it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across the full video latent to maintain both spatial and temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coherence, since frame-by-frame inpainting leads to temporal arti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: facts like flickering. In practice, this vanilla approach does preserve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original background alignment, however causes the masked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas to degrade into incoherent, temporally unstable blobs (Fig. 2a).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We attribute this breakdown to a core difference between image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and video models: image inpainting ensures spatial consistency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within a single frame, while video inpainting must also maintain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temporal consistency across frames. Unlike image inpainting, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relies heavily on hallucination, video inpainting must infer missing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content from both spatial and temporal context, making it signif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: icantly more challenging. We further examine a second zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inpainting method: Vid2Vid [HaCohen et al. 2024] (an adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from Img2Img [Meng et al. 2022]). This method applies heavy noise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inside the mask and lighter noise elsewhere in the latent video, then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denoises the entire latent. Vid2Vid effectively removes the target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object and synthesizes plausible fills, however, it also introduces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artifacts into the background and motion (Fig.2b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 5 Method: OmnimatteZero

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we first describe how given a video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use off-the-shelf video diffusion models to remove the target object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 5.1) and its associated visual effects (Section 5.2). Next, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detail our strategy for isolating foreground objects together with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their residual effects (Section 5.3). Finally, we demonstrate how to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recombine these object-effect layers onto arbitrary background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos (Section 5.4), enabling flexible and realistic video editing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, our pipeline expands masks to capture object effects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inpaints them for clean backgrounds, isolates foregrounds via latent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arithmetic, and seamlessly recomposes them onto new scenes.

layout_dets.text: 5.1 Object Removal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zero-shot video inpainting with diffusion models [Lugmayr et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2022; Meng et al. 2022] frequently struggles because the model must

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hallucinate content that is coherent both spatially and temporally (

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 3). Recent studies show that the self-attention mechanism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within diffusion models is crucial for maintaining coherence during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model generation [Luo et al. 2025]. However, it remains unclear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: how self-attention can effectively guide the inpainting process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: frames. This principle has been leveraged in traditional video editing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques [Criminisi et al. 2004; Wexler et al. 2004]. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they often produce non-realistic results or do not scale for long

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos. Motivated by this, we introduce a method that explicitly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guides a video diffusion model to reconstruct missing pixels by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model to infer this implicitly. To further enhance spatial inpainting

layout_dets.text: Alpha-Channel Extraction: The alpha-channel is obtained from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the soft mask Mi (Eq. 4) by decoding it with the video VAE using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only the spatial and temporal upsampling layers, skipping feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: re-encoding. This ensures (1) softness, the output remains a soft

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask that captures graded transitions around boundaries and effects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (2) alignment, the decoded alpha-channel is upsampled to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: original resolution, maintaining pixel-wise correspondence with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RGB frames. The result is a temporally and spatially consistent matte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that preserves soft boundaries, shadows, and reflections, enabling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: realistic compositing and evaluation.

layout_dets.text: 5.4 Layer Composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the object layers extracted, we can now seamlessly compose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them onto new videos by adding the object layer latent to a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background latent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specifically,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 5b (Latent Addition) illustrates the initial result with some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: residual inconsistencies, which we finally fix, by applying a 3 noising-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denoising steps. This process helps smooth transitions between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video background and foreground layers, resulting in a more natural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and cohesive video (Figure 5b Latent Addition + Refinment).

layout_dets.text: 6 Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following [Lee et al. 2024], we evaluate OmnimatteZero on three ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plications: (1) Background Reconstruction, where the foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is removed to recover a clean background; (2) Foreground Extrac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, where objects are extracted, together with their associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects (e.g. shadows and reflections); and (3) Layer Composition,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where extracted elements are reinserted into new backgrounds while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserving visual consistency. For qualitative results, each figure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows one representative frame per video; full videos are in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supplementary material.

layout_dets.text: 6.1 Background Layer Reconstruction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared methods: We conducted a comparative evaluation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our approach with several SoTA methods. These methods fall into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: four categories: (A) Omnimatte methods that are trained to de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compose a given video into layers: Omnimatte [Lu et al. 2021],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: D2NeRF [Wu et al. 2024], LNA [Kasten et al. 2021], Omnimat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teRF [Lin et al. 2023] and Generative Omnimatte [Lee et al. 2024].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B) Video inpainting methods that are trained to remove objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a video: RePaint [Lugmayr et al. 2022] adapted for video, Tem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poral Enhance [Luo et al. 2025] applied to vanilla inpainting (Sec 2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which enhances general temporal attention during denoising, Lu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: miere inpainting [Bar-Tal et al. 2024], Propainter [Zhou et al. 2023],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DiffuEraser [Li et al. 2025], and VideoPainter [Bian et al. 2025]. Fi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nally, (C) An image inpainting method that is applied for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video frame independently: ObjectDrop [Winter et al. 2024].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Datasets and Metrics: We evaluate our method on two standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Omnimatte datasets: Movies [Lin et al. 2023] and Kubric [Wu et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2024]. These datasets provide object masks for each frame and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground truth background layers for evaluation. All methods are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Quantitative results: Table 1 presents a comparison of Omnimat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teZero with the SoTA Omnimatte and inpainting methods on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Movies and Kubric benchmarks. It shows that OmnimatteZero out-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performs existing supervised and self-supervised methods designed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for object inpainting or omnimatte. It achieves the highest PSNR and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowest LPIPS on both the Movie and Kubric datasets, demonstrating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: superior background reconstruction. Specifically, OmnimatteZero

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [LTXVideo] achieves a PSNR of 35.11 (Movie) and 44.97 (Kubric),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surpassing Generative Omnimatte [Lee et al. 2024], all while re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quiring no training or per-video optimization. Notably, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement is not due to a stronger video generation model, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both OmnimatteZero and Video RePaint [Lugmayr et al. 2022] use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same generator, yet Video RePaint records the lowest PSNR and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highest LPIPS across all benchmarks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our method is also significantly faster. OmnimatteZero [LTXVideo]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runs at just 0.04s per frame (or 24 frames per second). These results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: establish OmnimatteZero as the first training-free, real-time video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matting method, offering both superior performance and efficiency.

layout_dets.text: 7 Conclusion and Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we introduced OmnimatteZero, the first training-free

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach for video omnimatte. By leveraging pre-trained video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diffusion models together with spatial and temporal attention guid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ance, OmnimatteZero enables real-time object removal, foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extraction, and seamless layer recomposition without any additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training or test-time optimization. Extensive experiments demon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strate that our method outperforms supervised and self-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: baselines in both background reconstruction and multi-object han-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dling, while achieving state-of-the-art runtime efficiency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nevertheless, several limitations remain. First, since our pipeline

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relies on VAE compression and decompression, the reconstructed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video may exhibit slight deviations from the original input. Second,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the quality of temporal correspondence depends on the accuracy of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TAP, which can degrade under heavy occlusions or in low-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos. Third, the fidelity of inpainting is ultimately bounded by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the capabilities of the underlying video diffusion model, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may struggle in highly complex or unfamiliar scenes. We believe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these limitations will be progressively mitigated as future video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generative models continue to improve in visual fidelity, temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency, and robustness. OmnimatteZero provides a fast, flexible,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and practical framework that can readily incorporate such advances,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paving the way for scalable, real-time video editing applications.
